accepted_input_states.raw_condition: a message arrived and reports fix_type < 3 -- the receiver is alive and says it has no position
no GPS_RAW_INT within 1.5x the nominal refresh period; absence has no in-band encoding and is a receiver-side timeout inference

allowed_merges.reason: once a value is older than the channel's max_age, 'never arrived' and 'arrived too long ago' both mean the consumer has no current measurement; no declared downstream property distinguishes them. FailsafePolicy reasons only over state.fresh (csia/runtime/failsafe.py:100).

forbidden_merges.needed_by: FailsafePolicy raises nav_degraded with the reason string 'GPS data invalid' whenever fresh['gps'] is false (csia/runtime/failsafe.py:145-152). If I and N are indistinguishable the recorded reason is a guess: a dead link and a receiver reporting loss of lock produce the same flight-log entry, and the diagnostic hypotheses they support are different (antenna/receiver fault vs telemetry path fault).

freshness.rule: a channel older than max_age is unusable and reported STALE

retention.rule: on an explicit no-fix report the retained position and velocity are discarded rather than allowed to age out

sentinel_handling.rule: an in-band no-value report is recorded with its own reason, not the default

diagnostic_visibility.rule: the reason a channel is unusable must reach a consumer that can act on it differently from any other reason
